The Terraform behind this week

week-09-container-apps — what each file does, and how big it actually is
week-09-container-apps/
│
├── terraform/
│   ├── versions.tf          41   # azurerm, the HCP backend, and a SECOND
│   │                             # provider aliased to sub-management
│   ├── variables.tf         70   # image, replica floor and ceiling, and why
│   │                             # each default is the default
│   ├── main.tf             154   # resource group, identity, environment, app
│   ├── logging.tf           78   # reads week 08's workspace across a
│   │                             # subscription, routes two log categories
│   └── outputs.tf           36   # the FQDN the tests call, and the workspace
│
└── scripts/
    ├── deploy.sh            73   # registers Microsoft.App and WAITS for it
    ├── validate.sh         282   # 6 checks. #3 polls until replicas hit 0,
    │                             # #4 times the request that pays for it
    └── cleanup.sh          103   # deletes the group, then verifies against
                                  # Azure that week 08 is still standing

# 5 resources, and the split follows the subscription boundary
#
# main.tf answers "what runs, and how little of it runs when nobody is
# asking" -- the environment, the app, the replica floor of zero and the
# ceiling that stops zero turning into a runaway bill.
#
# logging.tf answers "where does it report, and does that cross a boundary"
# -- and it is a separate file because the answer lives in another
# subscription. The workspace is READ, never owned: a data source cannot be
# destroyed by this week's teardown, which is the property that makes one
# shared workspace safe to depend on.
#
# versions.tf carries two provider blocks for the same reason. A provider is
# pinned to one subscription, so reaching across is a declared relationship
# rather than a pasted resource ID.
